title: Exact finite-valued functors on finite continuous group sets are forgetful
statement: Let $G$ be a topological group. Let $\mathcal C_G$ be the category whose objects are finite sets with a continuous left $G$-action (each finite set has the discrete topology), and whose morphisms are $G$-equivariant maps. Let $U:\mathcal C_G\to\mathbf{Sets}$ send an action to its underlying set. If $H:\mathcal C_G\to\mathbf{Sets}$ preserves finite limits and finite colimits, that is, is exact in the sense of [def-galois-exact-functor], and $H(S)$ is finite for every $S\in\mathcal C_G$, then there exists a natural isomorphism $U\xrightarrow{\sim}H$.

proof.text: Finite limits in finite actions remain continuous: the stabilizer of a limit point is the finite intersection of the stabilizers of its coordinates. For a finite colimit each point is the image of a point in a diagram object, so its stabilizer contains an open subgroup and is open. The full subcategory of continuous actions therefore inherits these limits and colimits, and the underlying finite-set functor preserves them.

For an injective equivariant map, the complement of its image is invariant. Its inclusion is injective, so its point stabilizers agree with those in the ambient continuous action and are open. It gives the complementary summand required by Mathlib PreGaloisCategory. Quotients by finite groups are finite colimits after shrinking the indexing group to a finite type in universe zero. The underlying finite-set functor reflects isomorphisms, since an equivariant bijection has an equivariant inverse. Thus it is a fibre functor and the category is Galois.

Exactness [def-galois-exact-functor] sends nonempty actions to nonempty sets. Indeed the map from a nonempty action to the terminal action is epic (its underlying map is surjective). Preservation of pushouts preserves epimorphisms, so its image is an epimorphism onto a singleton. Consequently an object with empty image is empty and hence initial.

If H(f)=H(g), the equalizer inclusion e of f and g has isomorphic image by equalizer preservation. Write its target as the coproduct of the equalizer and its invariant complement Z. Coproduct preservation and the surjectivity of H(e) force H(Z) to be empty. The preceding step makes Z initial, so e is an isomorphism, giving f=g. Hence H is faithful. The category is balanced: the faithful underlying-set functor preserves finite limits and colimits and reflects isomorphisms, so the Mathlib balanced-of-preserves criterion applies. A faithful functor out of a balanced category reflects isomorphisms.

Lift H to finite sets using the given finiteness instances. The inclusion of finite sets into types reflects finite limits, finite colimits and isomorphisms, so the lift is exact and reflects isomorphisms. It preserves quotients by finite groups by the same shrinking argument. It is therefore a Mathlib fibre functor. Apply [lem-wf-fibre-functor-uniqueness] to this functor and the underlying finite-set functor, then whisker their natural isomorphism with the inclusion into types.
